To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the associations of six sports with all-cause mortality and cardiovascular disease ( CVD ) mortality were different for different sports.
participation in specific types of sports was associated with a reduced risk of mortality in the general population.
participation in swimming, racquet sports and aerobics was significantly associated with reduced risk of all-cause mortality and CVD mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the associations between specific types of sports/exercise and mortality risk in a pooled Scottish and English cohort.
the long-term effects of different types of sports on mortality.
the health effects of participation in specific types of sports/exercise and their associations with all-cause mortality and CVD mortality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the benefits of physical activity for health and well-being are well established.
participation in sport and physical activity is associated with lower all-cause and disease mortality.
participation in sport and exercise has been shown to have a beneficial effect on all cause and cardiovascular mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
swimming, running, football, racquet sports, aerobics and cycling are all good for you, but some more than others.
participation in sport is good for you.
participation in sports such as cycling, swimming and racquet sports may reduce the risk of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health benefits from sports and physical activities are not the same for all disciplines.
there may be some sports that are more beneficial than others.
the health effects of sport are not uniform and that the health benefits of sport participation are dependent on the type of sport being performed.
